subject: community-medicine
title: School health and adolescent health: high-yield essentials for NEET-PG

steps.tx: School health services aim to keep children healthy so they can learn. The **school teacher** is the most important functionary in school health services, while the medical officer supervises. Medical examination of children is done at the time of entry and thereafter at intervals, and the older school health committee advised every 4 years, whereas NRHM recommends every 6 months. Know both figures for exams.

steps.tx: A **healthful school environment** has specific norms. One urinal serves 60 students and one latrine serves 100 students. A classroom holds at most 40 students, with at least 10 square feet per child. Combined door and window area should exceed 25 percent of floor area, and desks should be of the minus type, where the chair edge sits inside the desk edge.

steps.tx: Adolescence is the period from 10 to 19 years, youth is 15 to 24 years, and young people span 10 to 24 years. Under the **Kishori Shakti Yojana**, adolescent girls aged 11 to 18 years receive support for nutrition, health, literacy and vocational skills. The **Rajiv Gandhi Scheme for Empowerment of Adolescent Girls** (SABLA) covers direct cash transfer to girls.

steps.tx: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare launched the **weekly iron and folic acid supplementation** programme to tackle anaemia among adolescent girls and boys. The Ministry of Women and Child Development administers the Nutritional Programme for Adolescent Girls. Remember which ministry owns which programme, since exams test this directly.
